_why: DECLARED DNS NAMES that viewer/auto.crt must carry, as DATA rather than as literals in code.
The generator adds, on its own, every IP this box actually holds plus loopback, the machine's
own hostname, and the Tailscale MagicDNS name read live from `tailscale status`. This file is
only for names the box cannot discover about itself -- the LAN zone names and the public
name that resolves back to the estate.
It exists because gen_auto_cert.ps1 used to hard-code ONE address (10.190.245.196) and mint a
cert valid for 3650 days. On 2026-08-03 that cert was 21 days old, covered exactly one of the
THREE network planes this box sits on, and could not regenerate for another ten years. A laptop
that moved from the Kilig LAN to the P-Zin WLAN could not open https://<wifi-ip>:8443/ at all:
the address was reachable (measured -- an established inbound TCP session from that same laptop
was live on another port at the time) but the certificate had never heard of it.
Adding a name here does NOT make it resolve. DNS is a separate concern. This only ensures that
IF a name resolves to this box, the TLS handshake succeeds instead of hard-failing.
